rationale:
Amended 4 Oct at his call: Wednesday 7 Oct goes back to intervals - 4x1km at 5-mile pace, the lighter end, turning easy if he feels rough on the day - and 14 Oct now builds on it to 5 reps. He is overruling the HRV caution for Wednesday, which the brief now lets him do (principle 3b); the risk, stated once, is that if the HRV slide is illness arriving, intervals are what would tip it. The Saturday gate stays in, at his choice, and he will read it on Friday.

Amend: one change, the Saturday 10 Oct gate. Previously an unexplained low HRV/RHR on Friday turned Saturday's tempo into easy running; now it shortens it to 2x8 min at the same pace, because you feel fine and a flat morning alone should not cost the whole session. Everything else stands, and here is why. Wednesday stays easy: HRV 32-35 for a week against a ~40 baseline, RHR 48-49 against 46-47, in a light week with no note to explain it, then a 9/10 race on top. Feeling fine is not the evidence that matters, because the achilles history was four years of feeling fine until it wasn't. The cost of waiting is three days on a session 4 weeks before Guy Fawkes. Easy running is untouched. Weeks 2-3 are unchanged and provisional. Your corrections on the record: the half prediction is 1:22:09, not a minute slower (1:22:23 before Cheltenham, 1:22:06 on 27 Sep); your lactate finish was a deliberate sprint to beat a bottleneck and I withdraw that criticism; and your Cheltenham pacing was even, which I had understated.

changes.notes: Rest - the normal Monday, and the day after a 9/10 effort.

Easy 7km, conversational, no strides. HRV has slid from ~40 to 32-35 over the last 10 days and the race has just added to it, so this is a recovery day in all but name. If a leg gym session is due, this is the day for it - after the race rather than before.

Restored at his call (overruling the HRV caution, 4 Oct): 3km warm-up, 4x1km at 3:38-3:40/km with 90s jog recovery, 3km cool-down, ~11km all in. Purpose: first sharpening session for Guy Fawkes - race-specific economy at 5-mile pace (the record is 3:38/km). Energy system: VO2/lactate-tolerance edge, short of a full VO2 session. Expected feel: controlled, comfortably hard, RPE an observation not a target. Recovery cost ~2 days, which still leaves Saturday clear. Deliberately 4 reps not 5: three days after a 9/10 race and with HRV sliding, this is the lighter end; 14 Oct builds to 5. HIS CONDITION: if he feels rough on the day - or fails the neck check (chest, temperature, aches) - it becomes easy 8km + strides instead, no discussion needed.
Easy 7km, Nike Vomero Plus.

Easy 5km, short. Gate for Saturday, read on Friday morning: if HRV is still at or below ~34 or RHR 49+ with no explanation in your notes, Saturday runs as a reduced tempo (2x8 min, ~10 km all in) rather than the full 3x8. Feeling fine counts for something, so it is a reduction and not a cancellation. Ill, achilles above 0, or first-step stiffness: Saturday becomes easy running.

Re-opening the spine, gently. 3km warm-up, 3x8min at threshold (3:52-3:55/km) with 2 min jog between, 3km cool-down, ~12km all in. Purpose: lactate-threshold work, aerobic-dominant, the foundation under the 5-mile pace work that follows. Expected feel: comfortably hard; RPE is an observation, not a target - on pace is the right session. Recovery cost modest. Progression: first quality since Cheltenham beyond the race and the 200s. Endorphin Speed 5. Run it on pace, not under it. If the Friday gate trips: 2x8 min at the same pace, ~10 km all in, same session just less of it.
Long run 15km genuinely easy (~5:00/km or slower), aerobic volume, ~75 min. One gel halfway (22g) for practice, not need. No pace work. The 30km+ ground belongs to the winter block.
Provisional — Rest. Normal Monday.
Provisional — Easy 8km, conversational.

Provisional — 5-mile pace work: 3km warm-up, 5x1km at 3:38-3:40/km with 90s jog recovery, 3km cool-down, ~12.5km all in. Purpose: race-specific VO2/economy at Guy Fawkes pace (the record is 3:38/km). Feel: hard but controlled. Recovery cost ~2 days. Progression: one rep more than 4x1km on 7 Oct, same pace. HRV and how 7 Oct went decide whether it stays at 5.
Provisional — Easy 7km. Leg gym fits here.
Provisional — Easy 6km.
Provisional — 3km warm-up, 2x15min at threshold (3:52-3:55/km) with 3 min jog, 3km cool-down, ~13km all in. Progression from 3x8min: same pace, longer reps.
Provisional — Long run 16km easy (~5:00/km). One gel at ~40 min for practice. No pace work.
Provisional — Rest.
Provisional — Easy 8km.

Provisional — Last interval session: 3km warm-up, 6x600m at 3:32-3:36/km with 2 min jog, 3km cool-down, ~11.5km all in. Purpose: speed just above race pace so 3:38 feels controlled on the day. Short reps keep the cost low. If pace_target.json has flagged by then, the paces tighten.
Provisional — Easy 7km. Last heavy leg session of the block belongs this week or early next - nothing heavy after Wed 28 Oct.
Provisional — Easy 6km + 4-6 strides.

Provisional — Last hard session, 8 days out. 3km warm-up, 2x2 miles at 5-mile race pace (3:40/km) with 3 min jog, 3km cool-down, ~14km all in. Rehearsal of Guy Fawkes pace, on pace not under it. Nothing hard follows until the race.
Provisional — Easy 12km, no gel needed. Seven days clear of the race, so genuinely easy and short. Race week gets written next Sunday.
